destinations.title: N=4 EFT constraints and conditional Veneziano selection
destinations.question: Which nonlinear four-point Wilson-coefficient relations follow from N=4 supersymmetry, unbroken SU(4) R-symmetry, higher-point tree factorization and six-scalar parity, and what numerical selection of the four-gluon open-superstring amplitude follows after separately imposing dispersive assumptions?
destinations.summary: New explicit replacement for c0 and c1. UV-independent EFT relations precede a separate numerical bootstrap that suggests selection of the Veneziano amplitude with appropriate four-gluon kinematic prefactors. Neither convergence nor uniqueness is proved here.

systems: Non-gravitational, weakly coupled, planar four-dimensional EFTs reducing to N=4 super Yang–Mills at leading low-energy order
targets: Nonlinear relations among four-point Wilson coefficients of Tr D^(2k) F^4 operators and their supersymmetric partners
Conditional numerical selection of the open-superstring four-point tree amplitude: the Veneziano amplitude with kinematic prefactors appropriate to four-gluon scattering
regimes: Single-trace four-, five- and six-point tree amplitudes
Separate numerical four-point bootstrap with an arbitrary but nonzero spectral gap
assumptions: N=4 supersymmetry and unbroken SU(4) R-symmetry
Standard tree-level factorization on massless poles for four-, five- and six-point amplitudes
Parity-even six-scalar amplitudes, excluding local contact terms containing Levi–Civita contractions
For the bootstrap stage only: unitarity, analyticity and A4/s² → 0 as |s| → ∞ at fixed u < 0 or fixed t < 0
conventions: The EFT stage assumes neither properties nor existence of a UV completion.
The large-energy condition is stated for the source's four-point amplitude A4; the candidate retains the four-gluon kinematic prefactors.
The candidate curve is parameterized by string tension relative to the assumed spectral gap, following the source's convention.
includes: The Coulomb-branch example as a boundary of the parity assumption: its reported massive-W one-loop correction gives incompatible coefficients, and its six-scalar amplitudes require Levi–Civita-bearing local terms.
excludes: A proved uniqueness theorem or universal uniqueness of string UV completion
Applying the nonlinear coefficient constraints after admitting parity-odd local six-scalar terms
Importing dispersive or UV-existence premises into the EFT stage
Inferring inconsistency of Coulomb-branch N=4 SYM from failure of the parity-restricted constraints
Identification of Wilson coefficients with Wilson lines
